title: Uneven quota-buckets and UI lag causing per-model cost underreporting
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Customers and internal dashboards show persistent underreported per-model costs for bursts that hit quota/rate-limiter thresholds. Symptoms include (1) sudden dips in per-model tokens and cost lines at the same time as rate-limit responses, (2) overall account-level usage still reconciling to expected totals, and (3) Console charts smoothing that hides short-lived backfills. This ticket investigates the interaction between quota-bucket eviction logic, rate limiter early-drop behavior, and the ingest pipeline that powers per-model breakdowns in the Console.
observed_behaviour: Per-model cost series show 30-90s gaps for customers with bursty traffic (observed across 3 accounts).
Account-level token counters reconcile to billing sink totals but per-model charts are lower by ~6-12% in the last 24h window for affected customers.
Rate limiter returns 429 with X-Quota-Bucket header for many of the dropped requests; those drop events sometimes are not present in the per-model ingestion stream.
Console chart smoothing and a 1-minute rollup hides short backfills causing operations to miss incidents.
A recent change to quota-bucket TTL and eviction (runtime-1.18) coincides with first reports.
Backfill jobs run later reconcile totals but do not populate model-level tags consistently, leaving gaps in per-model dashboards.
impact_analysis: Customers with bursty workloads (streaming generation, high-concurrency webhooks) see underreported per-model spend in Console but are billed correctly from account-level billing sink.
Platform teams may miss regressions in model-specific cost/latency if console data does not surface drops tied to quota throttles.
Operational confusion: alerts tied to per-model thresholds didn't trigger due to missing spikes that were rate-limited at the edge.
hypotheses: Hypothesis A: Rate-limiter early-drop path skips adding a 'rate_limited' event to the model-tagging pipeline, so dropped requests never surface to per-model rollups.
Hypothesis B: Quota-bucket eviction (TTL) clears model attribution keys before telemetry flusher persists them, producing orphaned token events attributed to 'unknown' or dropped entirely.
Hypothesis C: Backfill reconciliation job (late_ingest_normalizer) merges events but strips custom model metadata when events arrive via fallback sinks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Spin up a dev account with model X and generate bursts (10 concurrent requests each 200 tokens) to hit rate-limit thresholds within 60s.
2) Observe rate-limiter 429 responses and capture X-Quota-Bucket headers and request IDs.
3) Check per-model console chart for model X for 5-minute window; compare to account-level token sink (billing-export).
4) Run the same burst but with quota-bucket TTL extended in staging; compare per-model visibility.
investigations: 2026-03-10: Initial triage by Ava Chen. Collected affected accounts and example request IDs; confirmed account-level sink matches billing export (so invoicing unaffected).
2026-03-11: Engineering spike by Marco Alvarez to trace 429 path. Added debug logs to rate-limiter that show early returns skipping telemetry enqueue. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3214)

2026-03-12: Identified a race between quota-bucket eviction and telemetry flusher: eviction GC removes model attribution key for short-lived ephemeral API keys used by some customers. Added unit tests reproducing eviction window. (Test branch: github.com/redwood/telemetry/tree/eviction-race)

2026-03-13: Confirmed that backfill/normalizer job re-ingests events but a recent transform strips 'model_ref' when events arrive over the fallback path (legacy-field-mapping change). Opened PR to preserve model_ref. (PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/987)
2026-03-14: Staging deploy with telemetry enqueue on early-drop path and patch to normalizer merged to staging; running e2e bursts to validate.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Short-term mitigation: Add telemetry enqueue for rate-limited requests to capture 'dropped' events with full model metadata. Low-risk and quick rollback. Chosen as immediate fix (approx +0.5% telemetry QPS).

Medium-term: Increase quota-bucket TTL for ephemeral keys from 30s -> 90s to reduce eviction races. Tradeoff: slightly higher memory for quota buckets under extreme scale. Plan: make TTL configurable per-tier and monitor.
Long-term: Rework fallback ingestion path to preserve model_ref and stabilize backfill dedup semantics. Requires careful rollout and integration tests.
action_items: ENG: Merge and deploy rate-limiter telemetry enqueue (owner: Marco Alvarez).
ENG: Patch normalizer to preserve model_ref for fallback events (owner: Priya Rao).
ENG: Add end-to-end test that hits rate-limiter and verifies per-model ingestion (owner: Marco Alvarez).
PM: Communicate incident and mitigation plan to affected customers and update docs about short-term visibility delays (owner: Lucas Green).
SRE: Monitor memory impact of TTL increase and add alerts for quota-bucket cardinality (owner: Samir Patel).
Design: Update Console tooltip to call out 'short-lived rate-limited drops may be backfilled' to reduce confusion (owner: Priya, Design).
acceptance_criteria: Staging: Per-model console charts show no gaps for 5 bursts test (10 concurrent requests x 200 tokens each) within 30m after change deployed.
Prod: No more than 1% discrepancy between account-level billing sink and sum of per-model costs attributable to dropped events over a 24h window for affected customers.
Backfill job: Normalizer preserves model_ref for fallback events demonstrated by unit tests and before/after runs for sample dataset.
Monitoring: Alerts in place for quota-bucket cardinality and ingestion lag >60s for model-tagged events.

notes: Do not conflate this issue with billing sink undercounts — this is primarily a per-model visibility problem caused by telemetry attribution and backfill transforms.
Cross-team coordination required between runtime, ingest, SRE, and Console frontend to ensure UI surfacing meets acceptance criteria.
